state.para: Every enumeration is a subscription of its own: it subscribes when it starts and unsubscribes when it ends, by , an exception or cancellation, which throws . The loop body runs on the context of the enumerating code, not on a thread of the SDK.
Only the latest value the consumer didn't read yet is kept, older ones are skipped. The enumeration ends when the SDK ends the subscription, for example because its owner was disposed.

stream.para: Every enumeration is a subscription of its own: it subscribes when it starts and unsubscribes when it ends, by , an exception or cancellation, which throws . The loop body runs on the context of the enumerating code, not on a thread of the SDK.

Every value is kept until the consumer reads it, the buffer grows while the consumer is slower than the SDK. The enumeration ends when the SDK ends the subscription, for example because its owner was disposed.

disposable.para: The values hold native resources: dispose every value you receive, including the elements of arrays and tuples. Values that weren't yielded are disposed for you.
